newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips, Thomson, Siemens in x-ray technology pact.
newsitem.headline: Philips, Thomson, Siemens in x-ray technology pact.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Tuesday it had formed a venture with units of France's Thomson SA and Germany's Siemens AG to make digital detectors for x-ray imaging systems.

The new venture, called TRIXELL, will be based in Moirans, France, and majority owned by Thomson through its Thomson Tubes Electroniques subsidiary. Philips Medical Systems and Siemens Medical Engineering will each hold 24.5 percent.
The detector developed by TRIXELL is designed to improve clinical care and lower costs by allowing standard radiographic procedures to be digitised, Philips said in a statement.
The first TRIXELL product will be released next year and will be a digital, solid-state flat device using amorphous silicon technology and digital signal processing.
The products will be the result of pooled research from the three companies and also include research undertaken within the Eureka and Esprit programmes which began in 1989.

"The goals of the three partners in TRIXELL are to share the development and the industrialisation costs of this new detector family, as well as to facilitate its marketing in the international medical, industrial and scientific sectors to all manufacturers," Philips said.
